approved: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2013

Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment Bill, noting it largely repeats Labor's lapsed 2012 legislation, including allowing travel expenses for veterans' treatment to be approved before or after travel, and extending Defence Service Homes Act benefits to personnel who served aboard HMAS Canberra during Operation DAMASK VI, but warned Labor would be vigilant against any hidden cuts to veterans' entitlements.

Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment Bill, noting the department processed more than 165,000 claims for travel expense reimbursements in 2012-13, and highlighted his electorate's Anzac Centenary commemorations including the Kangaroo March re-enactment and a bid for grant funding to build a statue of Victoria Cross recipient Private Ryan.

Welcomed the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment Bill and reaffirmed the coalition's commitment to fairly index DFRB and DFRDB military superannuation pensions, benefiting 57,000 superannuants, and highlighted $410,000 in Veteran and Community Grants funding for projects including Men's Sheds upgrades.

Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment Bill and praised The Long Way Home, a theatre production developed with the Sydney Theatre Company in which wounded or ill Australian Defence Force personnel perform their own stories on stage as part of their rehabilitation.

Supported the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment Bill and read extensively from a letter by Atomic Ex-Servicemen's Association president Reuben Lette describing being ordered into nuclear fallout without protection during British atomic tests, noting a site clean-up completed in 2000 cost $108 million and that fewer than 700 test veterans remain alive.

Summed up the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2013, reaffirming the government's commitment to deliver fair indexation for DFRB and DFRDB military superannuants aged 55 and over from 1 July this year, and noted the department processed over 165,000 travel expense claims for treatment in 2012-13.
